texts.content_exam: In 1912, the "Titanic" hit an iceberg on its first trip across the Atlantic. The Titanic was the largest ship that had ever travelled on the sea. It was carrying 2207 people, but it had taken on enough lifeboats for only 1178 people. Not more than 651 of the passengers were able to get into lifeboats. Some of the survivors had been in the icy water for hours when they were saved. Most of the passengers hadn't lived long; 1502 people had lost their lives. But why was there such a great loss of life and so few survivors who were on the edge of death? Nobody had prepared for such a tragedy. Nobody had believed that the Titanic could sink. The steamship company had thought that its ship would be completely safe in all situations.

questions.question: The "Titanic" hit ......... on its first trip across the Atlantic.
The Titanic was the largest ......... that had ever travelled on the sea.
Not more than 651 of the passengers were able to get into ......... .
Nobody had believed that the Titanic could ......... .
The steamship company had thought that its ship would be completely ......... in all situations.

texts.content_exam: Nobody had believed that the Titanic could sink. The steamship company had thought that its ship would be completely safe in all situations. They had followed an old rule for the number of lifeboats, so they had supplied lifeboats for only half the people. The passengers had not yet received their lifeboat numbers, nor had they practiced lifeboat drill before the accident. Many of them had not even dressed warmly, the ship had hit the iceberg late at night, and they did not believe they were in danger. The ship had already received 6 ice warnings on its radio when it struck the iceberg. Nevertheless, it had not changed its direction or its speed. A tragedy like the sinking of the Titanic should never happen again.

questions.question: The passengers had practiced lifeboat drill before the accident.
The ship had received 6 ice warnings before it struck the iceberg.
The Titanic changed its direction after receiving ice warnings.
Why didn't the passengers believe they were in danger?
questions.explanation: ✅ الإجابة الصحيحة: Because the ship hit the iceberg late at night, and they did not believe they were in danger.

questions.question: What important lessons did the Titanic disaster teach the world?
questions.explanation: ✅ الإجابة الصحيحة: lessons about safety at sea and preparedness

texts.content_exam: Frane Selak was born in Croatia in 1929. He led a relatively unremarkable life as a music teacher. Selak's near-death experiences began in January 1962 when he was travelling by a train from Sarajevo to Dubrovnik. The train left its railway tracks and ended up in a river. Fortunately, an unknown person pulled him to be safe, while 17 other passengers drowned. The next year, Selak boarded a plane from Zagreb to Rijeka. Unfortunately, he was blown out of its door and luckily landed in a haystack; the plane crashed, killing 19 people but Selak survived. Three years after that, in 1966, he got on bus. The bus skidded on the road and fell into a river, drowning four passengers, and by sheer luck Selak swam to the shore with only a few cuts and bruises.

questions.question: Frane Selak worked as a ......... .
The train left its railway tracks and ended up in a ......... .
Selak survived the train accident because an unknown person ......... .
questions.explanation: ✅ الإجابة الصحيحة: pulled him to safety

questions.question: On the plane, Selak was blown out of its ......... .
The plane crash killed ......... people.

texts.content_exam: In 1970, the fuel in his car's tank exploded on the motorway. But Selak just escaped with his life. The final famous disaster was in 1996 when a truck came barreling towards his car as he was driving around a mountain road. Selak was ejected from the car but he managed to hold onto a tree, and watched his car in horror plummet down. In 2003, two days after his 73rd birthday, Selak won the lottery in Croatia. With this, he bought a luxurious home. Then he changed his mind, sold it in 2010 and lived a humble life with his fifth wife. What happened to Selak seems to be far more dramatic than anything Hollywood could cook up. Suppose it is true, still we can't tell whether he is the luckiest or the unluckiest man in the world. Whatever happened along the way.

questions.question: Selak won the lottery in 2003.
Selak bought a small house after winning the lottery.
questions.explanation: ✅ الإجابة الصحيحة: False (He bought a luxurious home).

questions.question: Selak's story is less dramatic than a Hollywood movie.
What did Selak do after winning the lottery?
questions.explanation: ✅ الإجابة الصحيحة: He bought a luxurious home, then sold it and lived a humble life with his fifth wife.

questions.question: Is Selak the luckiest or unluckiest man in the world? Why?
questions.explanation: ✅ الإجابة الصحيحة: We cannot tell - he survived many accidents (lucky) but faced many near-death experiences (unlucky).
